name: research
trans: n. systematic investigation to establish facts; a search for knowledge

name: project
trans: n. any piece of work that is undertaken or attempted; a planned undertaking

name: programme
trans: n. an announcement of the events that will occur as part of a theatrical or sporting event

name: proposal
trans: n. something proposed (such as a plan or assumption); an offer of marriage

name: procedure
trans: n. a particular course of action intended to achieve a result

name: allocate
trans: v. distribute according to a plan or set apart for a special purpose

name: reference
trans: n. a remark that calls attention to something or someone; a short note recognizing a source of information or of a quoted passage

name: laboratory
trans: n. a workplace for the conduct of scientific research

name: equipment
trans: n. an instrumentality needed for an undertaking or to perform a service

name: microscope
trans: n. magnifier of the image of small objects

name: development
trans: n. act of improving by expanding or enlarging or refining

name: stage
trans: n. any distinct time period in a sequence of events; a specific identifiable position in a continuum or series or especially in a process

name: phase
trans: n. any distinct time period in a sequence of events

name: monitor
trans: v. keep tabs on; keep an eye on; keep under surveillance

name: record
trans: v. make a record of; set down in permanent form; register electronically

name: label
trans: v. assign a label to; designate with a label; attach a tag or label to

name: diagram
trans: n. a drawing intended to explain how something works; a drawing showing the relation between the parts

name: analyze
trans: v. consider in detail and subject to an analysis in order to discover essential features or meaning

name: analysis
trans: n. an investigation of the component parts of a whole and their relations in making up the whole

name: finding
trans: n. the act of determining the properties of something, usually by research or calculation; the decision of a court on issues of fact or law

name: presentation
trans: n. the activity of formally presenting something (as a prize or reward); a show or display; the act of presenting something to sight or view

name: topic
trans: n. the subject matter of a conversation or discussion; some situation or event that is thought about

name: survey
trans: n. a detailed critical inspection; short descriptive summary (of events)

name: journal
trans: n. a daily written record of (usually personal) experiences and observations; a periodical dedicated to a particular subject

name: discussion
trans: n. an extended communication (often interactive) dealing with some particular topic; an exchange of views on some topic

name: outline
trans: n. the line that appears to bound an object; a sketchy summary of the main points of an argument or theory

name: structure
trans: n. a thing constructed; a complex entity constructed of many parts; the manner of construction of something and the arrangement of its parts

name: content
trans: n. everything that is included in a collection and that is held or included in something; what a communication that is about something is about

name: introduction
trans: n. the act of beginning something new; the first section of a communication

name: overview
trans: n. a general summary of a subject

name: background
trans: n. a person's social heritage: previous experience or training; the part of a scene (or picture) that lies behind objects in the foreground

name: summary
trans: n. a brief statement that presents the main points in a concise form

name: conclusion
trans: n. a position or opinion or judgment reached after consideration; an intuitive assumption

name: round off
trans: v. make round

name: slide
trans: n. a small flat rectangular piece of glass on which specimens can be mounted for microscopic study

name: illustration
trans: n. artwork that helps make something clear or attractive; showing by example

name: handout
trans: n. an announcement distributed to members of the press in order to supplement or replace an oral presentation

name: note
trans: n. a brief written record; a short personal letter

name: eye contact
trans: n. a meeting of the eyes between two people that expresses meaningful nonverbal communication

name: audience
trans: n. a gathering of spectators or listeners at a (usually public) performance; the part of the general public interested in a source of information or entertainment

name: body language
trans: n. communication via the movements or attitudes of the body

name: style
trans: n. how something is done or how it happens
